content.text: Section 24 fully matches our preferred position, and § 24.3 is scoped to "other assignments" so it does not override the § 24.1 carve-out.

input.quote: 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.
input.rationale: Section 24 meets the preferred position in full. § 24.1 lets us assign to an Affiliate (as defined in § 1.1) or an M&A/asset-sale successor without Vendor consent, subject only to prompt notice and assumption of obligations. § 24.2 binds Vendor asymmetrically: no assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without our prior written consent (reasonableness qualified only in Vendor's favour on capability/financial standing), and never to a direct Customer competitor. § 24.3 is expressly scoped to "other assignments," so the residual mutual consent requirement does not swallow the § 24.1 carve-out. § 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on our change of control and requires cooperation with successor administrative changes. § 13.3 aligns licence transfer with a Section 24 permitted assignment and limits Vendor's revocation/suspension rights. No change-of-control termination or re-pricing right appears elsewhere; § 9.2 is a standard insolvency clause that expressly excludes a lawful non-impairing reorganization. No redline needed.
